strengths: Addresses a timely, important problem in a rapidly growing field with strong motivation for taxonomy unification
Comprehensive systematic methodology covering 134 papers across 9 databases with clear inclusion criteria and multi-dimensional analysis
Well-structured taxonomy with useful novel distinctions (in-generation, in-context attribution) that effectively organizes fragmented literature
Extensive evaluation analysis of 300 metrics categorized across 7 dimensions and 6 methods, identifying fragmentation in common frameworks/benchmarks
Practical resource compilation (231 datasets, 17 frameworks, 11 benchmarks) with promised public release provides genuine community value
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (taxonomy diagram, evaluation metrics overview) that communicate complex information well
Systematic methodology following established guidelines (Petersen et al. 2008) demonstrates rigor in conducting the survey
weaknesses: Limited critical evaluation beyond description: no assessment of which approaches perform best, lack of tradeoff analysis (cost vs. accuracy, coverage vs. precision), and minimal discussion of failure modes or approach limitations

Shallow analysis of key findings: field dominance patterns (126 non-parametric vs. 25 parametric papers) unexplored, extreme framework fragmentation (only 2 reused) not critically examined, concentrated dataset usage not discussed as limitation

Questionable categorization scheme: distinction between Model-Centric (3 papers) and Data-Centric (4 papers) poorly justified, with both involving learning modifications; sparse category populations question meaningfulness of distinctions

Novelty primarily organizational: taxonomy heavily builds on prior work (Huang and Chang 2024), identified gaps are somewhat obvious, and solutions in Section 7 remain largely prescriptive statements rather than actionable insights

Evaluation analysis limitations: 300 metrics cataloged but missing validity/reliability analysis, no guidance on metric appropriateness for different tasks, Figure 7 dense and difficult to parse, complementary metrics concept underdeveloped

Search strategy and scope constraints: limited to three keywords (citation, attribution, quote) potentially missing related work using different terminology; February 2025 cutoff with only 10 papers limits trend claims; no analysis of literature biases across languages/domains/geographies

Absent empirical comparisons: no systematic comparison of methods on common benchmarks, no cost-performance analysis, missing guidance for practitioners on methodology selection, no discussion of approach performance across LLM scales

Methodological transparency gaps: inter-annotator agreement not quantified, annotation scheme details sparse, limited discussion of annotation bias or disagreement resolution; reproducibility concerns despite promised public release

strengths: Comprehensive systematic mapping study across 134 papers, 9 databases with clear methodology following established guidelines (Petersen et al., 2008)
Timely response to rapidly growing field: 86% of papers published after 2023; captures recent developments in evidence-based text generation
Useful unified taxonomy organizing seven attribution approaches, LLM integration strategies, five citation characteristics, and six tasks—provides valuable reference framework for fragmented field
Detailed categorization of 300 evaluation metrics across seven dimensions and six methods, identifying that only two frameworks/benchmarks are widely reused (highlighting standardization gap)
Well-organized presentation with clear sections and helpful visualizations; promise to release annotated dataset enhances reproducibility
Expansion of parametric attribution into three subtypes (Pure LLM, Model-Centric, Data-Centric) and identification of in-generation and in-context attribution as emerging approaches adds nuance
weaknesses: Limited novelty: Paper is primarily descriptive catalog of existing work lacking critical analysis of why certain approaches work, when to use them, or fundamental research bottlenecks

Shallow analysis of identified findings: High concentration on QA (71%), post-retrieval (73%), and zero-shot prompting (58%) noted but implications not explored; parametric attribution gap identified but not analyzed

Taxonomy lacks validation: No inter-rater agreement statistics reported despite dual annotation; no analysis of coverage completeness, categorical boundary justification, or alternative organizations considered

Evaluation analysis insufficient: Figure 7 extremely dense and difficult to interpret; no systematic comparison of metric appropriateness across tasks; why certain metrics/frameworks dominate unexplored

Methodological limitations: Simple keyword-based search may miss related work using different terminology; no sensitivity analysis of search strategy; no analysis of papers spanning multiple categories or addressing category overlap

Lack of actionable insights: No guidance on selecting approaches for specific tasks, missing discussion of computational efficiency, cost-benefit trade-offs, or multilingual applicability; no best-practice recommendations

Shallow Discussion section: Identified challenges (parametric attribution, evaluation standards, explainability) are somewhat obvious; limited engagement with fundamental questions about field maturity and research directions
Missing critical perspectives: No user studies on actual system usage; limited discussion of failure modes, negative applications, or why certain modalities (graphs 4%, visuals) are underexplored
Presentation issues: Main taxonomy (Figure 4) difficult to parse; dense sections enumerate rather than synthesize; could better distinguish from existing RAG and hallucination surveys

strengths: Timely and comprehensive systematic survey of 134 papers addressing the important problem of verifiable and traceable LLM outputs at a critical moment in field evolution (86% of papers from 2024)

Novel unified taxonomy that consolidates fragmented terminology by expanding parametric attribution into three types and introducing new categories (in-generation, in-context), providing valuable organizational framework for the field

Extensive and systematic analysis of 300 evaluation metrics categorized across 7 dimensions and 6 methods, with important finding that only 2 frameworks/benchmarks see reuse despite metric proliferation
Rigorous systematic mapping methodology following Petersen et al. (2008) with clear inclusion criteria, multiple database searches, and dual independent screening
Clear presentation and effective visualizations (especially taxonomy in Figure 4) that make complex information accessible to readers
Tangible resource contributions including promised release of annotated dataset and comprehensive supplementary tables supporting reproducibility and future research
Balanced coverage of diverse attribution approaches (post-retrieval, post-generation, in-generation, in-context) with specific concrete examples
weaknesses: Limited novelty beyond organizational consolidation—the taxonomy, while useful, primarily reorganizes existing concepts from prior work (Huang & Chang 2024, Li et al. 2023) rather than introducing fundamentally new insights

Surface-level analysis despite comprehensive scope: identifies important gaps (e.g., only 7 parametric attribution papers, low framework reuse) but provides limited analysis of why these gaps exist or how to address them

Inadequate discussion section (approximately 2 pages) for a survey of this scope—lacks deep synthesis, critical analysis of fundamental limitations, and concrete actionable recommendations for advancing the field

Severe task distribution skew (71% of 134 papers focus on QA, vs. 15 papers on grounded generation, 14 on summarization) that is reported but not analyzed for implications, potentially biasing evaluation metrics and frameworks toward QA-specific approaches

Incomplete analysis of critical gaps: parametric attribution identified as understudied (7 papers) but paper doesn't explain why, what fundamental challenges exist, or what breakthrough approaches might look like
Missing practical guidance for practitioners: no comparison tables of approaches showing computational costs, latency, accuracy trade-offs; no guidance on which approach to use when

Evaluation metric analysis lacks depth: catalogs 300 metrics but doesn't analyze validity, relationships, correlation with human judgment, or why framework reuse is so low (only ALCE and G-Eval reused)

Limited critical analysis of field maturity despite 86% of papers being from 2024—doesn't assess whether growth represents fundamental breakthroughs or incremental improvements, or discuss field stability and evolution

Generalization concerns: heavy dominance of non-parametric approaches (126/134) may reflect publication bias; limited discussion of how findings generalize across LLM sizes, architectures, languages, and domains beyond Wikipedia/scientific/news
Inter-annotator agreement not reported for categorization of 134 papers; subjective categorization decisions could affect reproducibility (though promised dataset release partially mitigates this)

strengths: Rigorous methodology following PRISMA 2020 with excellent inter-annotator agreement (α=1.0 on screening, 0.77-1.0 on taxonomy)
Comprehensive and timely coverage of 134 papers across a rapidly growing field, with systematic analysis of 300 metrics, 231 datasets, 19 frameworks, and 11 benchmarks
Well-designed multidimensional faceted taxonomy that captures field complexity without artificial constraints across three orthogonal dimensions
Practical contributions including evaluation guidelines (Table 1) that usefully distinguish core vs. contextual dimensions and provide informed metric selection guidance
Clear presentation with effective visualizations (taxonomy, metric overview) and extensive appendices providing valuable detailed analysis
Publicly available annotated dataset and comprehensive resource compilation that will serve as reference for the field
Identifies concrete standardization gaps (only 2 frameworks reused despite 19 existing) with actionable insights for future work
weaknesses: Limited analytical depth: paper is primarily descriptive and cataloging; lacks causal analysis of why approaches are chosen, which work best, or systematic analysis of trade-offs

No experimental validation: lacks comparative effectiveness analysis, statistical significance testing of trends, or empirical comparison of approaches; claims about evaluation utility are not validated
Significant task representation bias: QA dominates with 71% of papers (95/134); findings may be heavily QA-biased with limited discussion of generalizability to underrepresented tasks

Shallow evaluation framework analysis: documents fragmentation (only 2/19 frameworks reused) but provides limited analysis of why, no recommendations for framework adoption, and missing design principles

Missing critical comparative analysis: no systematic comparison of citation style effectiveness, no cost-benefit analysis, no computational efficiency discussion, no error analysis of existing approaches
Limited quantitative analysis: no correlation analysis between evaluation dimensions, no metric clustering, no statistical testing of temporal trends, no analysis of dimension interactions
Reproducibility gaps: inter-annotator agreement computed only on 30/134 papers, disagreement resolution underspecified, some taxonomy ambiguities (e.g., passage vs. other citation styles)

strengths: Rigorous systematic methodology following PRISMA protocol with good inter-annotator agreement and sensitivity analysis
Comprehensive scope: 134 papers, 300 metrics, 19 frameworks, 11 benchmarks, 231 datasets with public release promised
Well-designed multidimensional taxonomy accommodating approaches that combine multiple mechanisms without artificial mutual exclusivity
Useful practical outputs including evaluation guidelines (Table 1) and metric selection guidance (Table 9)
Clear presentation of patterns through extensive figures and tables showing temporal trends and task-specific distributions
weaknesses: Limited novelty: taxonomy largely repackages existing frameworks (Huang & Chang 2024); analysis is predominantly descriptive without explaining root causes or implications
Lack of critical analysis: identifies problems (fragmentation, 300 metrics with only 2 reused frameworks) but offers no solutions; future directions simply restate limitations
Severe domain imbalance: 75% of papers focus on QA; most datasets are Wikipedia/scientific; findings may not generalize to underrepresented tasks and domains
Shallow evaluation analysis: 300 metrics cataloged but not evaluated against each other; no meta-evaluation or investigation of why frameworks are underutilized; metric validity unquestioned

Poor presentation and organization: 40+ pages of appendices suggest inadequate integration; disconnected sections; dense tables (7, 9-12) difficult to extract insights from; reads as data catalog rather than cohesive research
Missing practical insights: no computational cost/scalability analysis, no guidance for practitioners on which approach to use, limited user perspective on citation style effectiveness

Questionable scope: single search string limits coverage despite 4% sensitivity check; citation visibility dimension (4% of papers) may not warrant taxonomy inclusion; some categorizations lack justification
Insufficient inter-annotator agreement validation: parametric attribution unmeasurable (zero papers in sample), lower agreement for contribution type (0.73), only 30 papers checked for IAA

strengths: Rigorous systematic methodology following PRISMA protocols with perfect inter-annotator agreement (α=1.0) on screening and strong agreement (0.73-1.0) on annotation across all taxonomy dimensions

Comprehensive scope covering 134 papers, 300 evaluation metrics, 231 datasets, and 11 benchmarks with extensive sensitivity analysis validating search strategy (only 4% additional papers with expanded search)
Well-designed multidimensional taxonomy with clear extensions beyond prior work (parametric subdivisions, in-generation/in-context approaches) enabling flexible multi-label assignments

Actionable practical contributions including evaluation guidelines distinguishing core vs. contextual dimensions (Table 1) and comparative metric analysis with measured aspects and limitations (Table 9)

Insightful empirical findings: identifies 58% non-parametric dominance of post-retrieval, 96% text-only citations, 3.4-fold 2023→2024 growth, and critical gaps (parametric attribution stagnant, in-generation only 4%)
Excellent reproducibility with public annotated dataset, extensive methodological appendices, clear inclusion criteria, and transparent limitations discussion
High-quality presentation with clear hierarchical structure, informative visualizations, and balanced depth-accessibility trade-off appropriate for broad audience
weaknesses: Limited conceptual novelty—primarily organizes and incrementally extends existing categorizations (Huang & Chang 2024, Li et al. 2023a) rather than introducing fundamentally new frameworks or insights

Lacks experimental validation: no controlled experiments comparing attribution approaches, no empirical evidence about which metric combinations predict quality, no analysis of evaluation dimension correlations or metric reliability

Primarily descriptive rather than prescriptive—excels at 'what' and 'how much' but provides limited analysis of 'why' design choices dominate or 'what practitioners should do' beyond Table 1 guidance without empirical support

Identifies but doesn't resolve core fragmentation (134 papers but only 2 evaluation frameworks reused, 300 metrics with low adoption, 231 datasets with limited standardization)—diagnoses problems without proposing concrete solutions or investigating barriers

Significant dataset and evaluation biases: Wikipedia dominates (Table 12), limited specialized domain coverage (health/law/science), task-specific datasets not reusable, English-language restriction—impacts generalizability of findings

Incomplete methodological guidance: Table 1 lacks empirical validation, no analysis of dataset suitability for different evidence levels, missing investigation of metric trade-offs or parameter combinations for effectiveness

Limited depth in analysis: task section mostly confirms existing knowledge, citation frequency doesn't explain why multiple citations sometimes don't increase trust, no cross-dimensional correlations or method combination analyses
